name: Songun
summary: Songun ('military-first') is the North Korean state doctrine, proclaimed under Kim Jong Il in the 1990s, that gives the Korean People's Army priority in politics and resources and names it, rather than the working class, the main force of the revolution. It is justified as defence against US-led imperialism, fused with Juche self-reliance, one-party rule under a supreme leader, collectivist discipline, and the aims of a 'powerful and prosperous' socialist nation and Korean reunification.
scope: The official DPRK doctrine from about 1995 to the present as set out in Kim Jong Il's 29 January 2003 talk on the Songun-based revolutionary line and described by scholars Han S. Park and Byung Chul Koh. It treats the doctrine as an extension of Kim Il Sung's Juche line, not as a general theory of militarism or praetorian rule elsewhere. Many answers on issues the doctrine never addresses are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Overview, origins, figures, and the 2003 shift away from the working class as main force.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Songun state provides services to the people through the army and state, so free state care fits; but the sources do not discuss health policy, so this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The state sets wages in a planned economy and the sources never discuss a minimum wage, so the question barely applies.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Songun is framed as strengthening the socialist system under central guidance; Koh notes only limited lower-level economic innovation under central control.

public-ownership.rationale: Songun is defended as protecting the socialist system, in which the state owns industry; the 2003 talk treats the munitions and key industries as central.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The DPRK formally abolished taxes and has no wealthy class in official doctrine; the statement does not map onto Songun.

unions-good.rationale: Unions in the DPRK are party transmission belts; Songun doctrine says nothing of independent worker organizing, so no clear position.

property-fundamental.rationale: The doctrine rests on collectivist principle and socialist ownership, with the army and state overriding individual claims.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: a state-run economy under party-army control leaves no room for autonomous corporations, though the sources do not address regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Park describes the military as provider of food and services to the people, so cutting provision runs against the doctrine; welfare is not directly discussed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership is by the state and collective under party leadership; workers' own control is not part of Songun.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Park describes a society mobilised and watched by the military and militia, with obedience to authority as a core cultural trait.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the stress on discipline and military-style uniformity; drug policy is not addressed in the sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the state controls speech wholesale rather than targeting hate speech specifically.

strong-leader.rationale: The talk calls for single-hearted unity behind the Supreme Commander and describes the army as moving as one under his command.

state-harmful.rationale: Songun exists to strengthen the socialist state and the army as its core; the state is the instrument of the revolution.

limit-guns.rationale: Civilians are mobilised in the People's Militia while the state monopolises arms; the statement about civilian gun ownership does not fit cleanly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Military affairs are of paramount importance and the army must be strengthened in every way, with priority in resources.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the military-style discipline and uniformity Park documents; not directly addressed.

decide-locally.rationale: Authority is centralised in the leader and the army chain of command; Koh notes only limited low-level innovation under central guidance.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on class struggle and uncompromising treatment of the class enemy; penal policy is not addressed.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: Park notes cultural uniformity and obedience, and no sources endorse changing family forms; family itself is not discussed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the conformist military culture; not addressed in the sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in Songun texts; adherents' position cannot be inferred with confidence.

more-religion-public.rationale: The doctrine puts the Juche idea and the revolutionary soldier spirit at the centre of ideological life, leaving religion no public role; religion is not discussed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial injustice is not a Songun theme; its anti-imperialism is about national sovereignty.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The talk presents Songun as inspiring national independence, self-respect and pride, and says the revolution proceeds in the country's own way.

gradual-change.rationale: Songun frames politics as militant and revolutionary, but it also defends the established system, so this is an inference only.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the closed, self-reliant, sovereignty-first stance; immigration is not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The doctrine rejects outside interference and pressure and treats the world order as an imperialist offensive against the DPRK.

free-trade.rationale: Koh notes that the arms build-up needs foreign-sourced weapons and revenue, but the doctrine stresses self-defence and independence from external pressure.

nation-first.rationale: Songun is presented as politics of independence that resists outside interference and defends the country's sovereignty above all.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The talk condemns US imperialist aggression and encroachment on other countries' sovereignty, so intervention in the name of rights is rejected.

open-borders.rationale: The doctrine defends the sovereign, defended homeland and its border by force of arms; open borders contradict this.

limit-growth.rationale: The goal is a great, prosperous and powerful socialist nation, with an economic power built through science and technology.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not addressed by Songun sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The talk says the army's example can help the country conquer the fortress of cutting-edge science and technology and build an economic power.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not discussed, though Koh reports the nuclear deterrent as central to the security effort; the civilian question is inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The talk calls for completing the revolutionary cause by force of arms and defends the armed pioneering of the revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Park says the military leads and teaches society, yet also says ordinary people are supposed to take part in decisions; neither frames 'experts'.

central-planning.rationale: Koh describes economic management kept under central guidance with socialist principles retained.

socialized-markets.rationale: Koh notes some innovation and 'practical gains' in management but no principled embrace of market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax scheme of this kind has no place in the state-owned socialist order; not addressed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Private inheritance is not an issue in the doctrine; not addressed.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine ties benefit to labour and army service rather than unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from self-reliance and independence from foreign pressure; trade policy is not discussed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Park says the military sets policy goals and priorities for other institutions, and the army has top call on resources.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The system is collectivist and state-owned rather than a small-owner order; not directly addressed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The doctrine says class differences remain and the state must be strengthened; abolition of money is not part of Songun.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: a state-run economy keeps a state bank; not addressed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Wages and prices are set by the party-state, not by autonomous bodies bargaining; not addressed directly.

one-party-rule.rationale: The talk insists the revolution is guided by the Party and that the army becomes strong only under the leadership of the party and the leader.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Official doctrine rejects monarchy though it has a hereditary-style leadership succession; the doctrine speaks of leader and party, not monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Park says the military and leader are the legitimating centre of government, and the military is always right; electoral choice is not that source.

direct-votes.rationale: Park says people are supposed to participate in decisions but the centre decides; direct voting is not part of the doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: The talk explicitly ranks the army above the working class as main force of the revolution, which runs against rule through workers' bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: The doctrine's stress on national unity and reunification of one country rejects splitting it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Park reports the view that the military and the leader are uniquely fitted to lead; the 'natural' framing is not used.

political-violence-never.rationale: The talk says the revolution was won and defended by force of arms and that Songun requires smashing the enemy at all costs.

war-builds-character.rationale: The army's 'revolutionary soldier spirit' of self-sacrifice is held up as the model for all society, though war is cast as defensive.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred: the state ideology is secular and monopolises ideology; the doctrine says nothing of churches.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law and authority derive from the Party, leader and Juche idea; scripture plays no role.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence is the army's paramount mission and an affair of the state.

military-superiority.rationale: Military affairs are of paramount importance and the army must be strengthened in every way; the army is called invincible.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The doctrine speaks of the Korean nation and its unity; the sources do not discuss ethnic composition, so this is inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The talk calls for sharpening class struggle against the US imperialists and the class enemy, though it also demotes the working class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Park notes a pervasive sense of equality in official culture, apart from the leader; outcomes are not discussed.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The doctrine is militantly anti-imperialist, but reparations are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: The focus is a single Korean nation and national independence, not a civilisational bloc.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The doctrine rests on the collectivist principle and a self-sacrificing spirit as the model of behaviour.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The army's duty of defending the leader at the risk of one's life is held as the model for the whole people.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The doctrine seeks a powerful industrial nation and upholds modern science and munitions industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The talk wants advances in cutting-edge science but within the existing system, not disruptive acceleration.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Park places the military as the brain of the political system; algorithmic rule is not discussed.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the state-controlled information order and surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: Songun claims to continue Kim Il Sung's line while pursuing a new stage; split between continuity and progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Doctrine is explicit that the Juche idea and the Songun line are the guide, though it also claims to be proved by experience.

direct-action.rationale: The doctrine favours armed struggle over parliaments in revolution, but at home the state already holds power.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine aims to build a prosperous and powerful modern nation (s1), the opposite of a return to foraging, which no source discusses.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The talk keeps distinct roles for army, workers and farmers, noting class differences remain.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Official socialism is distribution by labour; need-based distribution is a distant communist goal, not Songun's concern.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist state production aims at serving the people and the army rather than profit, but it is not discussed in these terms.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The talk describes monopoly capital's domination and calls to end exploitation, in orthodox socialist terms.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Songun gives the army precedence over the working class and rejects the working class as the main force, though it keeps the class principle.

collective-farming.rationale: The talk notes cooperative farmers and a collectivist principle; Park reports soldiers doing farm work for the collective.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The talk says the world can never be at peace so long as imperialism remains rampant.

taxation-theft.rationale: The doctrine treats the state as the indispensable guarantor of the revolution.

harm-principle.rationale: The system demands total loyalty and conformity, not liberty limited only by harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The doctrine puts the collectivist principle above individuals and the masses' independence over personal claims.

conscription.rationale: Park reports a ten-year compulsory service and the mobilisation of nearly all able people in the militia.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The doctrine binds the people to the state and leader and rejects such a liberal check.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is the revolution's vanguard instrument, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The talk speaks of defending the people's independence and giving them affluent lives, but not in liberty terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: The military is held to be the real centre of power and opinion leadership, not media or universities.

organic-representation.rationale: The doctrine channels the people's unity through the party and army, not trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: Park describes the military shaping education, culture, daily needs and economic tasks as social engineer.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 'great, prosperous and powerful' nation is a goal reached after the hardships of the Arduous March, but decadence is not the theme.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The doctrine is framed as self-defence of the existing state, with reunification a separate aim.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The talk requires absolute loyalty to the leader, with the army defending him at the risk of life.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine is a modern socialist state, not feudal.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The doctrine states ideology and politics come first in education and that knowledge serves the party line.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is set by the revolutionary class principle and Juche idea.

single-common-good.rationale: The doctrine holds that all society shares one idea and faith and aims at a single united whole.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Management is under party and state leadership, not democratic votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is run by the state and the military; Park describes the Military University shaping the curriculum.

economic-freedom.rationale: The doctrine insists on socialist principles and central guidance; it holds that political independence rests on military power, not economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The army's soldier spirit is held up as the example all the people must follow, though force and law are also stressed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Songun is described as politics of independence defending the sovereignty of the country and nation.

force-without-un.rationale: The doctrine rejects outside authority over the DPRK's security, but it is framed as defensive and does not discuss UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The talk calls the doctrine scientific yet demands ideology and faith and conviction; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the closed, sovereignty-first stance.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred: labour is the basis of socialist distribution.

class-collaboration.rationale: The talk demands sharpening class struggle and uncompromising hatred of the class enemy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The doctrine honours the inherited revolutionary legacy; not directly addressed.

dominated-front.rationale: The talk says Songun inspires anti-imperialist independent forces worldwide against the imperialists.

workers-nation.rationale: The doctrine says nothing of organising workers either way; it relies on nation and army.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine's homogeneous national stress makes such law irrelevant.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The talk treats the state as a tool of the socialist revolution against class enemies, in orthodox terms.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Koh notes dependence on outside energy; self-reliance implies domestic production, but this is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from stress on uniform national culture.

proportional-representation.rationale: The legislature is subordinate to the leader and Military Commission; electoral design is not addressed.

national-mission.rationale: The talk presents Songun as an example stimulating the cause of making the whole world independent.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; official line holds equality has been achieved.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The doctrine stresses the unity of the leadership and people; it does not accept this charge.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The army is the revered core of the revolution, with no outside accountability for its past acts.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The military and state hold the centre of all areas of life.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The official line speaks of equality, but the army and leader are exalted above others; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The doctrine claims the DPRK builds socialism by itself, defended by its own arms.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the demand for national uniformity.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred: state schools teach the Juche idea and the army's ideology.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy comes from the military as centre and the leader, with the people said to support it absolutely.

trade-surplus.rationale: Koh notes the need for export revenue, but mercantilism is not a stated principle.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The doctrine holds that revolution and defence rest on force of arms and smashing the enemy.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Progress is attributed to unity of army and people under the party, not competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The one-party state forbids rival parties and demands uncompromising treatment of class enemies.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

separated-powers.rationale: Park cites the constitution making military and civilian sectors indivisible with the Military Commission issuing orders.

vanguard-party.rationale: The talk says the army and working class become revolutionary only under the leadership of the party and the leader, though it makes the army the main force.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed; priority goes to the military.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are not tolerated in the party-state; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Park stresses uniformity as a cultural strength; diversity is not discussed directly.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices follow party and army command.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Songun treats the situation as a grim war against imperialism, requiring militant ways.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from state-set prices in a planned economy.

party-controls-media.rationale: The talk demands strict ideological education and the party's control of ideology.

party-commands-army.rationale: The talk says the army is defended by party leadership, which has its firm place within the army, and political officers sit alongside commanders.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The talk requires carrying out the party's policies at all costs and stresses organization and discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The doctrine rejects outside interference and defends sovereignty through arms.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The army is united behind its Supreme Commander and moves under his command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority belongs to the party, leader and army.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The doctrine demands loyalty to the state and army.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Park says the military creates the norms and culture for society.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Koh notes Kim Jong Il held the top party post without regular election.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority flows down from the leader and military.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The doctrine rests on self-defence; it describes no alliance policy either way.

people-in-arms.rationale: Park reports that nearly all able people are mobilised in the People's Militia alongside a large standing army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The talk lists national reunification among Songun politics' aims, citing the June 15 Joint Declaration.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from uncompromising treatment of enemies; not addressed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The state ideology is atheist-materialist in tone; not addressed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from stress on the Korean nation.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Park lists uniformity and obedience to authority as cultural traits promoted by the military.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The talk ties independence to socialism and rejects pressure in the economy and politics.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution is a party-state instrument; not addressed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Park shows the military given primacy in guiding social and economic development, with obedience as the highest virtue.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Koh reports the North's claimed nuclear deterrent as the core of its self-reliant security effort.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Leadership is by party and army succession.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The party-state controls the economy and the banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is socialist and collective in service of the whole society.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The talk takes the Soviet collapse as due to imperialist pressure, not capitalist character.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

collective-defense.rationale: The doctrine is self-reliant and describes no alliance system.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from the state's ideological monopoly.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The leader is the supreme party and military leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on unity of the nation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The leader's cult is intense and loyalty is to be given at the cost of life, though not stated as divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

character-from-environment.rationale: The talk stresses remoulding of man through ideological education and class education.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Park notes the leader stands apart as the only non-equal figure and the military issues directives.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Authority is concentrated in one centre.

leader-cult.rationale: The talk requires single-hearted unity behind the leader and the defence of him at the risk of life.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The talk calls for sharpening class struggle under socialism, though it does not see party leaders restoring capitalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from agrarian collectivism; not addressed in the sources.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed beyond the single Korean nation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The talk says the materialist conception of history is limited and stresses ideological remoulding and the army's spirit.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Koh links self-reliance in national defence to the four-fold military line, though he notes it is hard to achieve.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

moral-incentives.rationale: The soldier spirit of sacrifice is the model, and ideological remoulding is placed ahead of other aspects.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national pride and independent ideology.

patriotic-education.rationale: The talk demands education of soldiers and people in the revolutionary soldier spirit and love of the country.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from state control of the economy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The talk holds that capitalism consolidates monopoly domination and imperialism and cannot bring lasting peace.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed. The Songun sources take no position, so the answer is neutral by default.

delink-world-market.rationale: Koh notes the self-reliance rhetoric; but the army's need for foreign-sourced arms qualifies it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The talk says workers have changed under capitalism but does not speak of a labour aristocracy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist, state-directed order.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The party-state is not limited by entrenched rights.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The talk says Songun must be held to constantly so long as imperialism exists, with the army and the state strengthened against the US-led encirclement.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's anti-imperialism and its view of Korea's division as imposed from outside.

elective-rulers.rationale: Leadership passes within the Kim family and loyalty to the supreme leader is a core principle.

minority-veto.rationale: Collectivist discipline and unity behind the leader leave no room for dissent to block decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Absolute loyalty to the leader is required, with no right of resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The party and army, not parliament, lead the state under Songun.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: animals are plainly used for food and the doctrine has no animal welfare concerns.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred split: duty is owed to the state and leader by all, not by a privileged class.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Political participation and ideological mobilisation are demanded of everyone.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: the state treats culture as a tool of mobilisation, and adherents would deny it pacifies.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine openly rests rule on army, party and the leader's authority, not on hegemonic consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-imperialism and self-reliance rest on viewing the world order as imperialist exploitation.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic, nationalist and closed character of the state.

party-own-road.rationale: Juche independence requires each party to find its own road without outside direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Juche self-reliance is the base of the doctrine, together with a self-sustaining economy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Reunification is a goal but not framed as recovery of lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine does not address it, and its nationalism is based on an ethnically homogeneous state.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: state legitimacy draws on the anti-Japanese guerrilla struggle, but no constitutional doctrine is described.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: the state would reject any condemnation of communism, and holds itself to be the socialist model.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the state views US history critically as imperialist and capitalist.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred split: it preserves its own monuments but removes colonial symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine centres on the military and national mobilisation, and not on gendered welfare programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: patriarchal state and militarised society make equal services unlikely.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Songun and Juche claim a Korean-style socialism fitted to national conditions, not foreign models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The doctrine places the army at the centre of politics as the main force of the revolution.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: the state mobilises women as labour and assigns care to family and state, with no wage for it.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: collectivist discipline and the Korean family-state ethos; sources do not address it directly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: cadre advancement runs on party and leader loyalty, not open competitive examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Self-reliance and central economic guidance imply state control over strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred: state and party regulate family life; sources are silent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: authority flows down from the supreme leader and party, not up from recall by electors.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Central economic guidance and state provision leave no place for private pension accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: socialist state ownership of land; sources do not state land tenure rules.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the constitutional order has a Supreme People's Assembly that formally approves the budget, though under party control.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from Park's account of cultural uniformity and national homogeneity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from self-reliance and the socialist state's ownership of land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine emphasises ethnic national homogeneity and rejects group-based remedies.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: stress on self-reliance and austerity against imperialist culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist line; the doctrine backs forces fighting imperialism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: doctrine of independence and anti-interference rejects great-power intervention, though it concerns itself with the DPRK.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's anti-capitalist, anti-imperialist framing; the sources do not discuss lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from Juche self-reliance and the siege framing against US-led imperialism, which treats foreign funding of civil society as subversion.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's aim of a 'powerful and prosperous' nation; the sources do not discuss birth rates.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of land and housing in the DPRK system; private purchase by anyone is not part of it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the socialist state's duty to assign work to every citizen; the sources do not discuss a job guarantee directly.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's view of the US as an imperialist aggressor that uses 'democracy' as a pretext.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist, supreme-leader system, where the law serves the revolution and the leader and obedience is owed to the party and army, not to law as such.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from Juche's stress on national sovereignty and independence; the doctrine's own defence of the DPRK rests on rejecting outside interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources do not address union structure; unions in the DPRK are state-run under party control, so the question barely applies.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's blaming of US imperialism and class enemies rather than a domestic minority; the sources do not discuss minority conspiracies.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist, family-and-nation-centred state, which has no place for abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from a one-party state that controls information and treats state matters as secret.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from Juche self-reliance, which favours domestic production and economic independence.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's army-led discipline and one-party rule, which leave no room for informal autonomous groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's absolute emphasis on national sovereignty over outside authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred from the DPRK's official secular ideology of Juche, which defines the nation by the leader, state and ethnicity rather than religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Songun is fused with Juche self-reliance and defiance of great-power pressure, so ritual submission and tribute to a leading power is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Economic guidance is centralised under the party and state, so regional retention of revenue is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: DPRK socialism holds the means of production in state or cooperative hands while allowing personal consumer property; inferred from the socialist-economy framework.

defeat-communism.rationale: The doctrine casts itself as the vanguard of a socialist revolution against imperialism, so a goal of defeating communism is the opposite of its position.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The state and party provide and direct services through the centralised system, leaving no role for private or independent providers; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Official Marxist-Leninist materialism treats religion as a product of social conditions; inferred, since the sources do not address religion directly.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Songun's anti-imperialist line treats capitalism's imperialist stage as an enemy; the Marxist stage theory gives a partial progressive role, so inferred and weak.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The state formally proclaims women's equality as part of socialist transformation; inferred from the socialist framework, not stated in the sources.

socialized-care.rationale: The collectivist socialist state favours public provision such as nurseries over private family work; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cultural uniformity and national purity are emphasised, consistent with the official policy of replacing foreign loanwords; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: A unitary one-party state would not see itself as bound by treaties with internal nations; inferred, as the issue does not arise in a homogeneous state.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The doctrine centres on the state, party and army under a supreme leader, not on small self-governing communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Korea is ethnically homogeneous with no minority-majority regions to settle, so the doctrine is effectively indifferent.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Songun presents itself as an extension of Juche socialism, so it rejects the idea that it is a third course between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The doctrine stresses Korean national unity and reunification, so claims of shared national and ancestral ties to land fit it; the sources do not discuss historical land claims, so inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine does not address it; the DPRK presents itself as anti-fascist, so denial is an unlikely position, but this is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The doctrine does not address it; collectivist discipline and conservative social norms of the state make acceptance of same-sex relations unlikely, but this is inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 2003 talk demands single-hearted unity behind the leader and party, and Park describes a system that tolerates no opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The doctrine does not address it; the state is atheist and subordinates other belief to leader loyalty, so punishing it fits, but this is inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism is central; the doctrine names imperialist domination as the enemy and demands national independence.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The doctrine backs armed defence against invasion but is secular and has no religious duty; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The state is atheist and rule rests on the leader and party, not on religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Songun puts decisions in the hands of the leader, party and army, not in direct popular decision-making, though it claims to serve the masses; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class struggle against imperialism and loyalty to the leader take priority; the doctrine does not discuss intersecting oppressions; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The doctrine does not address it; official conservative norms make legal recognition unlikely; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The doctrine does not address it; the collectivist state's emphasis on duty to the nation suggests rejection; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine rests on class and anti-imperialist struggle against the 'reactionary' West, so a left-right synthesis is not its view; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: As a socialist doctrine it sees capitalism as exploitative and the working masses as masters of their own work, but the sources never use alienation; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The doctrine is anti-Western but does not address Islam, and adherents have no stated position; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from the leader, party and army in a secular state, not from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The doctrine does not address it; a state demanding uniform loyalty is unlikely to allow religious dress in its institutions; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The doctrine has nothing to say on employment disclosure rules; indifferent.

social-market-economy.rationale: Songun upholds a state-run socialist economy with self-reliance and rejects market capitalism, though a 'prosperous nation' is an aim; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The doctrine's defining claim is the primacy of the army and military affairs, so abolishing armed forces is its opposite.

rich-first.rationale: The doctrine stresses collectivism and a unified planned state; the 'get rich first' idea is a different (Chinese) approach; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Juche self-reliance and independence from great powers fit staying out of rival blocs, though the DPRK has leaned on allies; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The leadership passed from Kim Il Sung to Kim Jong Il and then Kim Jong Un, and the doctrine is framed as continuing the line of the founding leader.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit is state-controlled in a command economy rather than owned by users; the sources do not discuss banking, so inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Juche self-reliance and defiance of US-led pressure imply rejecting outside economic conditions; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: The state claims universal participation under one party, so wealth tests are not part of it, though voting is not meaningful; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The sources do not discuss feminist or ecological theory, and the doctrine is indifferent to it.

reification.rationale: The state is socialist in name and criticises capitalism, but the sources do not discuss reification; neutral.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The state owns all media and venues and presents the capitalist press as propaganda; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule centres on the supreme leader's guidance and the army, not on standing law binding the ruler; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Scholars note an ethnic-nationalist strand tied to Korean unity, though formal citizenship is not racial; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: The state tightly controls the internet and does not allow public deliberation by citizens; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Secrecy around the leadership and military is central, so open records are not accepted; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The state is officially atheist and ignores religious law, so restricting interfaith marriage is not a goal; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: State ideology does not promote religious boycotts; inferred from its officially secular stance.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Songun rests on one-party rule under a supreme leader and army precedence, so decisions are not delegated to randomly chosen citizens; the sources do not discuss assemblies by lot, so this is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The doctrine is silent on religious law; the state subordinates religion to Juche and the leader, so neither preserving nor reforming doctrine is a stated position. Inferred, not sourced.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The sources do not discuss wealth concentration; the state denounces capitalist exploitation, but its own elite holds great privilege, so the position is split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: North Korea's official culture treats homosexuality as alien and the doctrine places the army as a disciplined collective; not addressed in the sources, so inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The state is officially atheist and suppresses religion in favour of the Juche cult, but it does not in practice run campaigns of atheist teaching; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Songun makes the army and security organs the main pillar of the state, so abolishing police and prisons is the opposite of its programme.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The doctrine is built on one-party rule under a supreme leader and the army, leaving no room for sharing executive power between communities; the nation is meant to be unitary.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Songun is a collectivist doctrine in which the state and army look after the people, rejecting reliance on private charity.

term-limits.rationale: The system is a hereditary supreme-leader state with no term limits, which they hold to be the basis of stability.

vote-delegation.rationale: Vote delegation conflicts with a one-party state under a supreme leader with unanimous elections; the doctrine provides no such mechanism.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The doctrine's priorities are national defence and a powerful state; existential-risk reduction is not addressed, though nuclear deterrence is held up as protection; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Official DPRK ideology claims women's equality, but the leadership and the army are male-dominated and religion is suppressed; inferred, not stated.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The DPRK law proclaims sex equality, but society and army remain patriarchal and the doctrine does not address marriage; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Juche self-reliance and wariness of foreign influence; the doctrine never addresses non-citizen voting.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the state-planned economy in which the state allocates housing; the doctrine does not discuss rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the collective, state-directed economy; the doctrine does not address patents, and adherents would likely keep state control of inventions.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Park describes the military as society's educator and social engineer, with universal conscription and militarised mass organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Scholars describe the nuclear deterrent as a pillar of the doctrine, so the DPRK keeps nuclear weapons on its own territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Kim Jong Il's talk frames the line as defence against US-led imperialism, which implies rejecting foreign (US) forces on Korean soil.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist stance, which condemns US wartime atrocities; the doctrine does not address genocide recognition directly.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The doctrine sits within socialist collectivism, where distribution follows labour and property income is rejected.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The doctrine makes armed struggle and the readiness to fight the core of the revolution, with no room for pacifist refusal.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from official nationalism that stresses Korea's long history and homogeneous people; the sources do not discuss it directly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's conventional state-socialist social line; it never addresses the question.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's indifference to feminist theory and its treatment of women as part of the unified collective.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the cult of revolutionary loyalty and the army's veneration of fallen revolutionaries; the sources do not use the religious wording.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from its materialist and secular official line; the struggle is framed as political and class-based, not spiritual.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the reunification aim, which seeks to gather the Korean people in one state rather than a dispersed diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the priority given to state and military power over cultural projects.

god-not-male.rationale: Official atheism and indifference; the doctrine does not address how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's control of ideology; the doctrine never uses women's full humanity as a test of tradition.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from official ethnic-nation ideology; the sources do not discuss minority groups.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Reunification of North and South Korea into one state for the Korean people is a stated aim of the doctrine.

independent-unions.rationale: The doctrine and party leadership put all organisations under the party and leader, so independent unions have no place.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Songun names the army, not the working class, as the main force of the revolution, so working-class power is not the test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The state controls the economy in a planned socialist system, so basic services are public; the sources do not discuss this directly.

second-chamber.rationale: The state is one-party with a single supreme leader and the sources describe no checks like a second chamber; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Property is held by the state and cooperatives, not by local communities; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The doctrine requires unified centralised leadership by the party and leader, so devolved confederal power conflicts with it.

family-wage.rationale: Wage policy is not discussed by the sources and the state sets wages in a planned economy.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation is not discussed by the sources; no position can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anti-ageing research is not discussed by the sources; no position can be inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The state tightly controls information and finances, so untraceable money would be incompatible; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: The state tightly controls communication and expects loyalty to the leader, so anonymity would be incompatible; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Juche and Songun stress collectivist discipline and loyalty to the leader, putting the person in service of the whole.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Juche stresses ideological consciousness as well as material life, and Park describes it in quasi-religious terms, but this is inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The state is unitary and centralised, so any regional powers would be delegated from above; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is not discussed by the sources; no position can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density is not addressed by the sources; no position can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: North Korean ideology stresses the unity of the Korean nation and its interests, but sources here do not discuss race; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: North Korean ideology takes pride in the Korean nation and its ancestry, but the sources do not address this directly; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Songun justifies the army as defence against imperialism, but the doctrine also aims at reunification, so it is split on this.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Songun doctrine treats Koreans as one nation divided by foreign powers and makes national reunification a central aim.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: a one-party state under a supreme leader has no place for separate religious electorates, and religion is subordinate to the party line.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Kim Jong Il's talk frames US-led imperialism as constantly plotting against the DPRK, which is the stated reason for military-first politics.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the DPRK officially claims free state education, but the sources do not discuss college tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address pollution policy; central planning and priority for the army would not favour taxing producers.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's 'prosperous nation' and revolutionary-succession language, which looks to future generations; no environmental stance is stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine glorifies the army and martial discipline and does not stress distinct female values in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: Military-first politics gives the army priority in resources and treats strong armaments as the guarantee of survival against imperialism.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: the DPRK conducts diplomacy through the leadership and the sources show no commitment to open treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Juche self-reliance and central control of the economy imply state control of what moves in and out of the country.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Korean People's Army is the core of the state and the revolution, so other armed groups would not be tolerated; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Songun places the army first and requires soldiers' absolute loyalty to the leader and the defence of the country; refusal to fight is incompatible.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions are party-controlled bodies and wages are set by the state, so independent collective bargaining is not part of the system; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The state does not tax households and top up wages in the capitalist sense; the doctrine prioritises the military and the state economy; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Songun puts defence spending first, so binding legal limits on state spending would be rejected; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The DPRK frames itself as anti-imperialist and in solidarity with the Third World, so it would favour rules that benefit developing nations; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Songun aims to defend and strengthen the existing socialist state under the leader, so smashing it is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The state-run economy under Juche and Songun allows no room for free economic experiment; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Nature as priced capital is a market idea at odds with state-run production; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Park describes the doctrine as tying the Korean nation and the leader into a single body whose survival gives members life's meaning.

student-debt-relief.rationale: There is no student loan system and the doctrine never addresses it; no stance can be inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The doctrine treats Korea as a unified nation and blames outside imperialist powers, not internal regions, for exploitation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Juche stresses remoulding the human mind to the revolution's ends, so human nature is not treated as fixed; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: The media are state and party organs with no independence; independent public media is rejected; inferred from the DPRK's system.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The state ideology of Juche and loyalty to the leader treats religion as subordinate to it; the one-truth claim is not addressed, so mild opposition is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Central economic guidance and state purchase of grain and collective farms fit state support for farmers, but the sources do not discuss farm price policy, so this is inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The doctrine sees a nuclear deterrent as the guarantee of survival against US-led imperialism, and the sources describe it as central to the powerful nation goal.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Korean Workers' Party rules as the only leading party under the supreme leader, and the doctrine names the army as the main force over the working class, so independent parties are rejected.

ban-fgm.rationale: The practice does not occur in Korea and the sources do not address it; inferred that a state with comprehensive legal control would readily prohibit it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The DPRK formally proclaims sex equality, but the sources do not discuss land or inheritance, and land is state-owned, so this is inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Songun's cultural unification and reunification aims imply one Korean language, and the DPRK treats it as one language; the sources do not discuss the question.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A centrally planned state economy with state ownership leaves no room for private tort claims against polluters; inferred from the planned economy.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Authority rests in the party and the supreme leader, and no role for customary chiefs is conceivable; this is inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The doctrine subordinates liberty to the leader and collective discipline, but its priority is military strength and development, not environmental protection, so the statement does not fit well.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A state of strict discipline and army-led social control would favour fixed legal penalties over independent judges, but the sources do not discuss sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The doctrine stresses cultural unity and the nation's language, but immigration is nearly nonexistent and the sources do not address it, so this is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Unions in the DPRK are state-run transmission belts of the party, so membership is compulsory; the sources do not discuss it, inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Elections are staged under one-party rule and ID checks are not discussed in the sources, so the statement barely applies.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The state keeps tight control of religion through approved bodies and puts the leader's thought above all creeds; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The doctrine claims its own system as the true people's democracy based on the leader and army, and rejects multi-party competition; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Socialist morality and collectivist discipline are stressed and sex outside marriage is socially frowned on in the DPRK; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The regime maintains total control of information and a closed national intranet, so cutting access is plainly acceptable to it; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: A planned, state-run economy with a leader-led distribution system leaves no room for a negative income tax; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The DPRK formally gave women equal voting and office rights in 1946, though real power is held by the leader and army; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Official Marxism-Leninist atheism treats religion as an old ideology that serves exploiters, so it is seen as a cause of oppression; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Juche stresses the unity and purity of the Korean nation, which cuts against treating race as a mere construct; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The DPRK has a state-aligned women's union that promotes official women's roles, so state bodies for women fit; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the DPRK holds land and resources as state or collective property, so private first-claim ownership is not recognised; the sources do not discuss it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's stress on sovereignty and defence against US-led imperialism; the sources do not discuss international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the state is officially atheist and its own ideology claims the central place; scripture is not discussed in the sources.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is a unitary, ethnically homogeneous nationalism under one leader, leaving little room for separate self-rule arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The doctrine defends the socialist state against imperialist attack with the army at the core, under one-party leader rule.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the Supreme People's Assembly formally chooses the top state offices, but the sources do not describe a council-delegate system.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: the state officially admits no rival to its own ideology and does not give any church legal primacy.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Korea is presented as one homogeneous nation under a unitary state, so ethnic territorial autonomy has no place.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: reunification is a state aim to be reached on the leadership's terms, not by a local vote; the sources do not discuss plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: reunification is a core aim, so inherited borders are not treated as fixed; Korea's division was not a colonial border.

simple-living.rationale: Self-reliance (Juche) and hardship for the revolution's sake are central, though the sources do not discuss simple living as a personal ideal; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is a unitary nationalism with no indigenous-majority regions, and the state controls settlement and residence.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the army is a model for society and mobilises all, and the DPRK has conscripted women, but the sources do not discuss it.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Songun is fused with Korean nationalism and Juche, treating the Korean nation and its territory as sacred to be defended.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the coercive one-party state and army priority; drug killings are not discussed in the sources.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: the 'powerful and prosperous nation' goal in practice relied on economic ties with China, though Juche stresses self-reliance.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's reunification aim and Korean nationalism; overseas minorities are not discussed.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the state controls all resources for the revolution and military, not as equal common ownership with compensation.

self-ownership.rationale: Juche and Songun subordinate the individual to the collective, the leader and the army, so full personal self-ownership is rejected.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not discuss consumption taxes, and a planned state economy gives no clear stance.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the state allocates services through the army and party by loyalty and priority rather than a scheme aimed at the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: power centres on the supreme leader, with party and army as his instruments; independent parties and groups are not allowed to mediate.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: military-first resourcing gives the army and favoured entities privileged economic position.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the one-party state tolerates no independent religious politics, so denominational politics is opposed.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: the powerful-and-prosperous-nation goal stresses science and technology together with Juche national tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the DPRK's formal commitment to women's equality in a socialist framework; divorce is not discussed in the sources.

national-resource-control.rationale: Self-reliance (Juche) and Kim Jong Il's line make national control of resources central to defending sovereignty.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: the state allocates wealth through planning and the army gets priority, so fairness is judged by state aims, not by how holdings arose.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine does not address international finance and the DPRK is largely cut off from it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address it; the DPRK denounces US racism but frames the main obstacle as imperialism.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: law is subordinate to the party and supreme leader, so a natural-law test against the state is not accepted.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine stresses mobilised labour and sacrifice for the nation, not working less.

multipolar-world.rationale: Songun is framed as defence against US-led imperialism, and the DPRK favours a world of independent sovereign states over a single dominant power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine descends from Marxism-Leninism via Juche, but the sources do not discuss value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine joins intense patriotism with a claim to serve working people, though it names the army, not the working class, as the main force.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is class and state centred and gives no weight to cultural identity politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the party and army rule, but the sources do not say how far markets are accepted; adherents prefer planned self-reliance.

missingStatements.text: The army, not the working class, should be the main force of the revolution.
missingStatements.rationale: The doctrine's defining claim is the 'precedence of the army over the working class' as the core and main force of the revolution.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Songun doctrine: no other ideology in the bank takes the opposite side except by implication, and every statement added must be answered by all future audits.

missingStatements.text: Military affairs should take priority over all other state affairs and resource allocation.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2003 talk says military affairs are of paramount importance and the army must be strengthened in every way.

missingStatements.text: The armed forces should serve as the model for civilian society, which should adopt soldierly discipline and spirit.
missingStatements.rationale: The talk says workers and all working people must learn from the revolutionary soldier spirit, and Park describes the military as society's educator.
missingStatements.declined: Too specific to Songun; the idea of soldierly discipline as a civic model is only partly covered by total-state and not worth another statement for all audits.

notes: Wikipedia and scholars describe Songun partly as a means of consolidating Kim Jong Il's power; this profile records the doctrine as its own texts state it. Kim Jong Un's later line is not separately profiled.
